newsitem.title: USA: Actor Reeve urges students to "show us the cures".
newsitem.headline: Actor Reeve urges students to "show us the cures".

text.p: Actor Christopher Reeve, paralysed from the neck down in a horse-riding accident two years ago, urged medical graduates Sunday to "show us the cures."
In his commencement speech at the Boston University School of Medicine, Reeve said efforts to conquer the afflictions of the body "will come to a standstill unless there is adequate funding."

"Government programmes that maintain survivors without doing more to help them are not acceptable. We must invest in the research that can and will give them reason to hope," said Reeve, who was awarded an honorary doctor of laws degree by Boston University.

The actor, who starred in the "Superman" series of movies, now often speaks on behalf of the disabled. He said he supports a bill to be introduced in Congress by Senators Tom Harkin of Iowa and Phil Specter of Pennsylvania which would help fund research.
The bill, the "National Fund for Health Research Act" would double the budget of the National Institutes of Health by deducting one penny for each dolllar paid in insurance premiums, he said.
"The insurance industry must have the vision; by spending one penny today they will be saving billions tomorrow," he said.
